main_text.p: Sequitur ex eadem Lege aliud Caput, quod ita habet: Rex, quisquis si erit, cum ΕΠΙΜΕΛΕΙΣΘΑΙ ΔΕ ΤΩΝ ΒΑΣΙΛΕΑ ΤΩΝ ΑΕΙ ΒΑΣΙΛΕΥΟΝΤΑ Paraficis, quos é singulis an- ΚΑΙ ΤΟΥΣ ΠΑΡΑΣΙΤΟΥΣ, ΟΥΣ na ei gentis populis, cum feni- ΑΝ ΕΚ ΤΩΝ ΔΗΜΩΝ ΠΡΟΑΙΡΩΝ- lus item, atque feminas uni- ΤΑΙ, ΚΑΙ ΤΟΥΣ ΓΕΡΟΝΤΑΣ, ΚΑΙ nis, curato. ΤΑΣ ΓΥΝΑΙΚΑΣ ΤΑΣ ΠΡΩΤΟ- ΓΟΝΕΙΣ.

Describit Athenaeus Lib. VI. ex Themistone in Paraphrasi ΤΩΝ ΘΕΣΜΩΝ ἐν Παναθηναίοις, ΓΙΝΕΣΘΑΙ ΔΕ ΤΩΝ ΒΑΣΙΛΕΑ, &c cetera, quae iam descripsimus. Caput de Legis Regiae attestatione Pollucis constat, vbi quid sit [?] interpretatur Lib. III. cap. III. [illegible, ~12 letters]. Sed inquiramus, de quibus hic agatur Sacris, quorum cura non tantum Regi, sed etiam Paraficis, Senibus, & feminis demandata est. Regis curae videntur fuisse communia Panathenaea: nam, vt est apud Pollucem Lib. VIII. cap. VIII. [illegible, ~10 letters]. Panathenaea autem erant in hoc censu. Panathenaeis praeterea Senes forma eximii eligebantur. Habes apud Xenophontem in Symposio: & ex eo Iuncus Libro de Senectute: cuius verba suo loco reddemus: atque hic [illegible, ~8 letters] inquit Iuncus. Hos Senes puto designari hac Lege ΚΑΙ ΤΟΥΣ ΓΕΡΟΝΤΑΣ. Quemadmodum & cum dixit, ΚΑΙ ΤΑΣ ΓΥΝΑΙΚΑΣ ΤΑΣ ΠΡΩΤΟΓΟΝΕΙΣ. intelligi puto anus illas, quae, quemadmodum Senes, in Panathenaeorum pompa oleae ramum gestabant: de quibus Dicaearchus in Panathenaico. Scholiastes Comici ad Vespas: [illegible, ~30 letters]. Atque de his tantum est.
Inter has Leges locum dedimus huic pfephifmati, quod vim Legis habuif- se nulli dubitamus.

ΤΑ ΔΕ ΕΠΙΜΗΝΙΑ ΘΥΕΤΩ Ο ΙΕ- ΡΕΥΣ ΜΕΤΑ ΤΩΝ ΠΑΡΑΣΙΤΩΝ· ΟΙ ΔΕ ΠΑΡΑΣΙΤΟΙ ΕΝΑ ΤΩΝ ΕΚ ΤΩΝ ΝΟΘΩΝ ΚΑΙ ΤΩΝ ΤΟΥΤΩΝ ΠΑΙ- ΔΩΝ ΚΑΤΑ ΠΑΤΡΙΑ. ΟΣ Δ' ΑΝ ΜΗ ΘΕΛΗ ΠΑΡΑΣΙΤΕΥΕΙΝ, ΕΙΣΑΙ ΕΓΩ [?] ΚΑΙ ΠΕΡΙ ΤΟΥΤΩΝ ΕΙΣ ΤΟ ΔΙΚΑ- ΣΤΗΡΙΟΝ. Sacerdos cum Paraficis men- strua facta facto. Paraficii de Nothis, aut Nothorum li- beris unum eligunto secundam morem patrium: si Paraficas- tudinem fuisse, in ius vocanto.
Meminit e Polemone Athenaeus Lib. VI. [illegible, ~40 letters]. ΤΑ ΔΕ ΕΠΙΜΗ- ΝΙΑ ΘΥΕΤΩ Ο ΙΕΡΕΥΣ ΜΕΤΑ ΤΩΝ ΠΑΡΑΣΙΤΩΝ·

page.notes: Page is heavily blurred and shows strong show-through from the reverse side, especially in the middle and lower Greek lines. Many Greek words and most Latin words in the central paragraph are doubtful; they are marked [?] or replaced by [illegible] where the letters could not be read. Right-margin notes are read from faint italic text and may be incomplete in wording. The line-end hyphens in the Greek block are printed hyphens. The page number and running head are read from the top of the page. The "M" at the foot is treated as a gathering signature.
